_comment: RESTAURANT CONCEPTS — what you are trying to be, as content rather than code.
These were hardcoded fixtures inside StrategyDiversity, where they were doing real work
(the whole distinct-winners measurement runs on them) while being invisible to the game
and impossible to mod. Architecture Rule 2 says content lives in data, and a concept is
content by any reading of it.
A concept is a CARD, a PRICE POSITION and HOURS. Deliberately no staffing, no equipment
and no floor plan: it says what you are attempting, not how well you execute it. Aaron's
bar is 'you should be able to win with any concept anywhere if you run the restaurant
properly', which only means something if running it properly is still the player's job.
Measured on tools/scout.js: these produce four distinct winners across the four US sites,
so which one suits a street is a real question rather than a cosmetic label.

concepts.name: Neighborhood standard
concepts.description: A short card of things people already like, priced a shade above the obvious. Hard to love, hard to get wrong.

concepts.name: Pizza and sharing plates
concepts.description: Two things, done fast and cheap. Families and locals; nobody comes for the wine list.

concepts.name: Fine dining
concepts.description: Expensive ingredients, long prep, and a price to match. Loved by more people than can afford it.

concepts.name: Coffee and counter
concepts.description: Breakfast and lunch, out fast. Lives or dies on whether anyone walks past before two.

concepts.name: Wine bar and small plates
concepts.description: A bar that feeds you rather than a restaurant that pours. Needs a liquor license before it is anything at all.

concepts.name: The whole card
concepts.description: Everything on the menu. Something for everyone, and a kitchen that pays for it in ticket time and mistakes.
